SMTO-LLM-0041 — The model's reply repeated the same detail twice

GUID: 20656f9a-3853-4fde-9ea1-625df8f2dcdc
Slug: duplicate-semantic-keys
Domain: LLM · Subsystem: llm

What happened

  • The model's reply listed the same piece of information twice, possibly with different values. SMTO didn't act on it, because it can't safely guess which one was meant.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Wait to see whether the Run continues. SMTO may ask the model once more by itself after a reply it can't use. The model may send a clean reply on its next try, without the repeated detail.
  2. If the Run stopped, read its activity in the conversation to see which steps already finished, then ask the Agent to continue only the rest. SMTO did not act on the confusing reply, but steps before it already happened. Repeating them could do the same work twice.
  3. If it keeps happening, ask the person who runs the model server to check its tool-call settings for this model, or choose a different model in Settings › Setup › Model routing. Repeated details come from how the model server formats replies, not from your request.

What success looks like

  • The Run continues past this step, and the Agent's next action appears in its activity.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them to the person who runs the model server or manages SMTO. Don't ask the Agent to redo steps that already finished.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • The model response repeats a key inside a semantic JSON object (choices, message, tool call, function or arguments), so normalization refused to pick a value by parser order.

What this means

  • Repeated keys in a semantic JSON object can assign conflicting meanings to one field; normalization refuses to choose a value by parser order. This category concerns model preparation or response acceptance. It does not reverse earlier operations or establish their outcome; their receipts remain authoritative.

Why this can happen

  • Repeated keys in a semantic JSON object can assign conflicting meanings to one field; normalization refuses to choose a value by parser order.

How to diagnose it

  • Inspect the provider's structured-output encoder for repeated semantic keys; repetition in ordinary text is a different issue.

How to fix it

  • Raised by unambiguous_object and json_object in src/agent_runtime/llm/openai_compat/response.py. Capture the raw provider response from the trace and fix the provider's structured-output or tool-call parser (or the chat template) so each key appears once; keep the rejection guard and do not replay completed operations.
  • Repair the provider’s structured-output encoding so semantic keys occur once. Keep the rejection guard; do not guess which duplicate value to execute.

Retry and execution caution

  • Correct the recorded cause, then inspect current state and existing receipts before requesting another attempt.

How to verify the fix

  • The same response structure contains each semantic key once and passes normalization.

What not to do

  • Do not replay prior successful operations to repair a later model response.
  • Do not disable protocol validation or treat this representation failure as input-context overflow.

Technical notes

  • This category concerns model preparation or response acceptance. It does not reverse earlier operations or establish their outcome; their receipts remain authoritative.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
